vm.qemu_environment_note: capstone_vm sets CAPSTONE_GP_NONLIN=1 and CAPSTONE_REV_NODES=65536; both are read only by QEMU's physical-profile paths (fabricated gp, internal revocation tree).
vm.share_model_why: the guest runs as root; with 9p security_model=none a file root creates on the share is the host user's, and perlbench's t/op/stat.t test 33 (-o) fails

Built in kit2/toolchain-v2 from 8f6b6c7d (same compiler sources, other docs) it was 71daa5aa...; both compilers produced byte-identical SPEC executables (q3 with v2, q4 with v3) and the same libc and SDK file count.

capstone-virtual.what: the profile as qualified: a lifetime per public object (CDERIVE on malloc, CREVOKE on free) and the payload zeroed on free

capstone-spatial-scrub.what: exact bounds, no lifetime per object, payload still zeroed on free: against capstone-virtual it isolates the lifetime machinery

capstone-spatial.what: exact bounds only: against capstone-spatial-scrub it isolates the free-time zeroing, against capstone-virtual the mechanism as shipped

arms_note: runcpu label -> SDK of recipes/sdks.sh; the key is the label and the SPEC executable suffix; capstone-virtual is the qualified configuration of q4 up to heap.c.obj
srcalt_note: packages/*.tar.xz are built from SPEC sources (tools/make-srcalt.sh) and never published; the sha256 files pin them; tools/build.sh reads them from CAPSTONE_SPEC_PACKAGES. srcalt-notes/ says what each package changes and why.
